items.title: EU Close to Deal to Link UK Carbon Market After Brexit Split
points: The European Union and the UK are in the final stages of a deal to link their emissions markets, a move that would boost liquidity and eventually save companies millions of euros in carbon border taxes.

The agreement, to be announced at a key summit later this month, would enable carbon permits to be traded across the two emissions systems, almost six years after Britain started its own cap-and-trade program in the wake of Brexit.
Started in 2005, the market imposes gradually shrinking emissions limits on around 10,000 facilities in sectors from steel and cement to fertilizers, power production and aviation.
While the EU carbon border tax became operational this year, with the first compliance deadline set for September, the UK mechanism is to kick off at the start of 2027.
The UK carbon contract for December closed at a £64.81 per ton on Friday while benchmark EU allowances were at €86.55.

points: Chennai, The Tamil Nadu government has dissolved the high-level committee on Centre-State relations headed by retired Supreme Court Judge Justice Kurian Joseph, citing overlap of mandate with the newly reconstituted State Law Commission.
The order, issued by Public Secretary E Sundaravalli on November 6, cuts short the panel's tenure six months before its final report deadline on May 31, 2027.

The three-member committee, comprising Justice Kurian Joseph, retired IAS officer K Ashok Vardhan Shetty, and former State Planning Commission chairman M Naganathan, had previously submitted the first part of its report to then Chief Minister M K Stalin in…
Because the Justice Kurian Joseph committee was non-statutory, its functions significantly overlapped with those of the newly empowered State Law Commission, the sources added.
A senior official, seeking anonymity, on Sunday said that administrative hurdles and internal "stepping down" also marked the closure of the committee.
According to him, following the TVK government assuming office, Naganathan resigned from the panel, while the government refrained from extending existing staff arrangements.

items.title: Toyota Develops New 1.5-Litre Hybrid Engine With 15 Percent Better Efficiency
points: Recently, the company announced that it is developing an all-new 1.5-litre four-cylinder petrol engine for its future hybrid vehicles.
What's interesting is that this new engine could offer over 15 percent better fuel efficiency than its existing hybrid systems.
Toyota has officially announced that it is developing an entirely new family of 1.5-litre four-cylinder petrol engines.

Toyota has also stated that the naturally aspirated version of this new 1.5-litre engine has been developed to cover the performance range currently served by its existing 1.8-litre hybrid engine and 1.5-litre three-cylinder engine.
This means that Toyota will eventually use this smaller four-cylinder engine in vehicles which currently require a larger 1.8-litre engine.
Toyota has stated that its next-generation hybrid powertrain is being developed to offer more than 15 percent better fuel economy compared to its existing systems.
If a hybrid vehicle currently delivers 25 kmpl, a 15 percent improvement would increase its mileage to around 28.75 kmpl.
Similarly, a car delivering 30 kmpl could theoretically return around 34.5 kmpl.

items.title: FSSAI seizes food items worth ₹81.8 crore, suspends over 1,100 licences in two-month enforcement drive
points: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) led an intensive nationwide inspection drive from September 1 to November 5, during which it seized more than 3,270 metric tonnes of food products worth an estimated ₹81.80 crore and suspended more…

In a series of posts on X, the food safety regulator said it had inspected 56,431 establishments and issued 10,047 improvement notices as part of the enforcement drive held across States and Union Territories in collaboration with State Food Safety…
It also collected 43,939 samples, of which 23,648 had been analysed.
Out of these analysed samples, 2,273 were found to be non-compliant with prescribed food safety standards.
Highlighting the scale of the operation, the FSSAI said it had suspended 1,133 licences and cancelled the licences of 52 food establishments.
Additionally, it also sealed 314 establishments and initiated 410 prosecutions.

items.title: ‘Growing a beard doesn’t make you Revanth Reddy’: Telangana CM takes swipe at KT Rama Rao
points: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday took a swipe at Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao for allegedly copying his looks, saying “simply growing a beard does not make you look like Revanth Reddy”.
Reddy also said political posturing without substance is like a fox trying to look like a tiger, and that mere imitation would not earn KT Rama Rao, popularly known as KTR, the trust of the voters.
Simply growing a beard does not make you Revanth Reddy.
Who knows how many more years it will take for him to gain some wisdom?" Reddy said, while addressing a gathering in Vikarabad.
"Until the leader changes the mindset, the people of Telangana will never trust (him),” he added.
He continued: "Even if you take 10 births or hang yourself from a toddy tree, you remain Taraka Rama Rao but cannot become Revanth Reddy in your life.

items.title: Body of Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota brought to Mansa for last rites
points: File. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13.

The party had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.

Congress received ₹281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to ₹517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held.

Historical trends indicate that markets have delivered average gains of around 0.5% in years when Muhurat Trading ended on a positive note, he said.

items.title: Sanskrit University suspension row: Govindan backs stir, says it should go on till suspended students write exams
points: Govindan on Sunday (November 8, 2026) expressed solidarity with the ongoing agitation by students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit at Kalady near Kochi, saying the protest should continue until all the suspended students are allowed to appear…
Sixteen students were suspended after a Students’ Federation of India (SFI)-led protest during a syndicate meeting on August 13 over a lack of adequate campus facilities.
They were accused of staging a “mock cremation” of Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas, manhandling her and attempting to damage university property.
A single bench of the Kerala High Court had directed the university to allow the students to appear for the examinations, but a division bench later stayed the order.
The students then approached the Supreme Court, which directed the single bench to decide the matter.
The university said the suspension of 10 of the 16 students would be revoked if they apologised, but they refused.

items.title: Rajasthan BJP MLA Jaswant Yadav dies at 73 after prolonged illness
points: BJP MLA from Behror and former Rajasthan Cabinet Minister Jaswant Yadav died in Jaipur on Sunday (November 8, 2026) morning after a prolonged battle with cancer.
Mr. Yadav breathed his last at 8.15 a.m., his son Mohit Yadav said in a social media post.

"It is with profound sorrow that I inform you that my revered father, Dr Jaswant Yadav ji, the current MLA from Behror, former Cabinet Minister in the Rajasthan government, and former MP from Alwar, is no longer with us," Mr. Mohit said.
He served as a minister in the Vasundhara Raje-led Rajasthan government from 2016 to 2018.
He began his political career in 1998 after winning the Assembly election from Mundawar.
Following his death, the strength of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly has fallen to 199.
According to the family, his mortal remains will be kept at his residence in Jaswant Nagar, Alwar, for public homage after 4 pm on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

items.title: Vijayan seeks roll back of Keralam circular allowing colleges to increase seats without govt nod, warns of commercialisation
points: LoP in the Keralam Assembly Pinarayi Vijayan on Sunday alleged that the state government's move to allow autonomous aided and self-financing colleges to increase seats without prior approval would lead to the commercialisation of education.
Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the government circular permitting the move, Vijayan said the decision had been taken under pressure from the managements of private colleges.

The CPI(M) veteran said a September 11 circular issued by the Higher Education Department had made prior government approval mandatory for introducing new courses and increasing seats in government, aided and autonomous colleges.

"The current provision that no government no-objection certificate (NOC) is required for starting unaided courses and increasing seats in autonomous aided and self-financing colleges is shocking," the former CM said.

He said allowing colleges to increase seats at their discretion, without assessing the necessity and disregarding existing regulatory mechanisms, would pave the way for the commercialisation of education.

PM Modi, Birla, Naidu among leaders who wish Telangana CM Reddy on 57th birthday
points: As Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy celebrated his birthday, leaders from diverse political factions came together to send their warm wishes.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared his greetings via social media and a heartfelt letter, to which Reddy expressed sincere gratitude.
The support from various state ministers and influential personalities underscores the spirit of political unity in the region during this special occasion.
